title: How AI agents actually use tools

creative_direction.core_message: A model never runs your tools; it asks your app to, in a loop you control.
creative_direction.viewer_benefit: Understand the tool-call loop well enough to add a first tool safely.
creative_direction.hook: Your AI agent doesn't run code. It asks your app to.
creative_direction.visual_identity: precise technical diagrams, code as typography
creative_direction.sound_design: soft UI ticks on reveals, low impact on the hook, ducked bed
creative_direction.call_to_action: Save this, and give your agent its first tool.

claims.text: Each tool is described with a name, a description and a JSON schema for its inputs.
When the model wants a tool, it stops and returns a tool call with the arguments it chose.
Your code runs the tool and sends the result back so the model can continue.
The Model Context Protocol standardizes how clients connect to tool servers.
Tool results should be treated as untrusted input.

scenes.narration: Your AI agent doesn't run code. It asks your app to.
scenes.heading: It asks your app
scenes.visual_intent: Create curiosity by correcting a common assumption

scenes.narration: First, you describe each tool: a name, a description, and a JSON schema for its inputs.
scenes.heading: Describe the tool
scenes.visual_intent: Show the shape of a tool definition as real code

scenes.narration: When the model wants a tool, it stops and returns a tool call with the arguments it chose.
scenes.heading: The model asks
scenes.visual_intent: Make the hand-off from model to app visible

scenes.narration: Your code runs the tool, sends the result back, and the model continues from there.
scenes.heading: The loop
scenes.visual_intent: The loop as three ordered steps

scenes.narration: Without tools, the model can only guess. With tools, it checks live data.
scenes.heading: Guessing versus checking
scenes.visual_intent: Contrast the two behaviours side by side

scenes.narration: The Model Context Protocol standardizes this, so one tool server can plug into many clients.
scenes.heading: One protocol
scenes.label: MCP
scenes.visual_intent: Hub and spokes: one protocol, many tools

scenes.narration: Treat every tool result as untrusted input, and require approval before anything destructive.
scenes.heading: Results are untrusted input
scenes.label: Safety

scenes.narration: Describe, call, run, return. Save this, and give your agent its first tool.
scenes.heading: Describe. Call. Run. Return.
scenes.visual_intent: Summarise the loop and loop back to the hook
